_about: Wire contract consumed by Milo-iOS (github.com/leodurandfr/Milo-iOS), a THIRD API client beyond frontend/ and Milo-Mac. Its consumers are short-lived processes — a WidgetKit timeline entry, App Intents — so there is NO WebSocket surface at all: everything is REST, and the app cannot be told about a change by the backend. If a route listed here is dropped, Milo-iOS breaks silently at runtime. THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH for that contract. test_milo_ios_contract.py enforces it offline on every pytest run: the backend still serves every route here, every route the VENDORED snapshot calls is declared here, the gap the other way is exactly `_pending_push`, and every payload_invariant holds against the typed response models. The non-blocking CI job check_milo_ios_freshness.py re-clones the real app and warns when vendor/milo-ios/ has fallen behind. Refresh the snapshot and this file TOGETHER, consciously, in one commit.
_why_this_exists: Not hypothetical. Commit cf430ae6 ('drop 3 Milo-Mac-only GET routes after Mac converged to /bulk') deleted GET /api/settings/dock-apps on the premise that Milo-Mac was its only consumer. Milo-iOS called it too, and still does in the published app (MiloAPIClient.getDockApps). The path survives for PUT, so the call answers 405, forever, with nothing anywhere reporting it. That is the whole failure mode this manifest turns into a failing test: a route with no caller in frontend/src/ is not dead, it is unwitnessed.

_snapshot.note: MiloAPIClient.swift names the routes; Models.swift names the response fields the app decodes. Every call goes through MiloAPIClient — the three Intents and the TimelineProvider build no URL of their own — so those two files are the whole surface.

_pending_push.why: The manifest leads the published app: these routes were integrated locally and verified against the unit on 2026-09-18, but are not in the pushed source, so the vendored snapshot cannot show them. They are listed so the manifest-vs-snapshot difference is enumerated DATA rather than a weakened assertion. test_pending_push_is_exactly_the_gap fails the moment the push lands and the snapshot is refreshed — emptying this list is how the contract completes itself, and it cannot be forgotten in silence.

_broken_calls.why: Calls the vendored app makes that the backend does not serve. They cannot be declared in `rest` — test_rest_route_exists would fail on a route that genuinely does not exist — and they cannot be ignored, or the contract would be silent about a client that is already broken. So they are listed, and test_broken_calls_are_still_broken fails the moment either side changes: if the backend starts serving it, or the app stops calling it, the entry is stale and must go. Same self-deleting shape as `_pending_push`.

routes.replacement: Read dock_apps.enabled_apps from GET /api/settings/bulk, already declared in `rest`. The path survives for PUT, which is why the call answers 405 and not 404.

rest.note: Body {delta_db, show_bar}. Built by hand with URLRequest rather than the get/post helper — the extractor reads both shapes on purpose.

Body {volume_db, show_bar?}. The ABSOLUTE global level. Clamped on volume_limits rather than rejected, so the response carries the applied dB and the client must read it back instead of keeping what it sent.
Body {mute} — `mute`, never `muted`. Response `mute` is read back from the derived state, so an online client that refused shows as false.
Body {volume_db}. MAC without colons in the path, with colons in every response. Answers 400 outside volume_limits instead of clamping — deliberately the opposite of PATCH /api/volume.
Body {delta_db} — a zone-wide DELTA applied atomically, emitting one volume_changed.
Also the ONLY read for dock apps: it carries dock_apps.enabled_apps. GET /api/settings/dock-apps no longer exists (cf430ae6) — that path serves PUT only and answers 405.
Answers 200 with status:'error' on failure, not an HTTP error — the same deliberate exception Milo-Mac depends on.
The single transport for every source command, play_context on music_library included. GET /api/audio/commands describes each source's table; do not hardcode one.
Called with ?favorites_only=true. The query is not part of the route identity.
Idempotent since 145e4876: with nothing playing it answers 200, where it used to serve an unguarded AttributeError as a 400.

payload_invariants._about: The response fields Milo-iOS reads by name. A route can survive while the field the app decodes is renamed, and a Codable struct that misses a non-optional key throws rather than degrading — which is how the published AudioStateResponse, declaring a non-optional `status` that /api/audio/state does not serve, fails every call. Checked against the typed response models, never against a hand-written copy.

schema._about: Dotted paths resolved through the live OpenAPI schema. `a.b` is a property, `a[k]` a dict value (additionalProperties).

builders._about: GET /api/multiroom/state types its clients and zones as Dict[str, Any] — opaque by design, since both carry computed and conditional keys. So its fields are checked against the functions that BUILD the payload, which is exact by construction where the schema says nothing.
